Duplicate records cost more than they look

Duplicates are the most expensive data quality problem because they hide inside totals. One customer under four spellings becomes four customers in your reports.

  • Inflated customer counts and wrong customer lifetime value
  • Duplicate marketing, billing and support contacts
  • Fragmented history, so no single view of the customer
  • Machine learning models that learn from repeated rows and overstate accuracy

Signs your data needs cleaning

  • Reports from two systems disagree on the same number
  • The same customer appears under several spellings
  • Dashboards break when a new date or category format shows up
  • Analysts spend most of their time fixing data before analysing it
  • Email campaigns bounce or reach duplicate recipients
  • Models perform well in testing but fail in production
  • Join keys fail to match across sources
  • Nobody can explain where a figure came from

§ 09Guide

Data cleaning explained: methods, steps and tools

What is data cleaning?

Data cleaning (also called data cleansing or data scrubbing) is the process of detecting and correcting inaccurate, incomplete, duplicated or inconsistent records so a dataset is accurate enough for analysis, reporting and machine learning. It is the most time-consuming part of data preparation, and the part that decides whether dashboards, forecasts and models can be trusted. Garbage in, garbage out.

Data cleaning for machine learning

Model quality is capped by data quality. Good data preprocessing handles missing values without leaking information from the test set, treats outliers according to domain knowledge, standardizes categorical labels, removes duplicate rows that inflate accuracy, and reviews label noise. We build these steps inside reproducible pipelines so training and production data are cleaned identically.

Data cleaning vs data cleansing vs data scrubbing vs data wrangling

How related data preparation terms differ
TermScopeTypical use
Data cleaning / cleansingFix errors, duplicates, missing values and inconsistenciesAnalytics and BI reporting
Data scrubbingDeeper, systematic pass including corrupt and legacy recordsMigrations and warehouse loads
Data wrangling / mungingCleaning plus reshaping, joining and enrichingDay-to-day analyst workflow
Data preprocessingCleaning plus encoding, scaling and splittingMachine learning
Data transformationChanging structure or format between systemsETL and ELT pipelines

The 7 steps of the data cleaning process

  1. Data profiling. Measure null rates, types, patterns and distributions.
  2. Data validation. Test records against business and integrity rules.
  3. Deduplication. Remove exact and fuzzy duplicates and merge to a golden record.
  4. Standardization. Normalize dates, units, addresses and categories.
  5. Missing value imputation. Fill or flag gaps using the right method.
  6. Outlier treatment. Correct, cap or keep anomalies with a flag.
  7. Monitoring. Keep a data quality scorecard and alerts running.

How to handle missing values: methods compared

Missing value imputation methods
MethodBest whenWatch out for
Listwise deletionFew rows missing, completely at randomLoses data and can bias results
Mean / medianNumeric column, low missingnessShrinks variance, hides relationships
ModeCategorical columnOver-represents the most common value
KNN imputationCorrelated features, moderate missingnessSlow on very large data, needs scaling
Regression / MICEMissing at random with strong predictorsModel assumptions, leakage if done before the split
Interpolation / forward fillTime series with short gapsWrong for long gaps or abrupt changes

§ 11FAQ

Data cleaning questions, answered

Data cleaning services find and fix errors in your datasets: duplicates, missing values, inconsistent formats, typos, outliers and invalid entries. The result is a clean, validated, analysis-ready dataset with a log of every change, so your reports, dashboards and machine learning models run on trustworthy data.

They overlap heavily. Data cleaning is the general term for correcting data errors. Data scrubbing usually describes a more thorough, systematic pass, for example before a data migration or warehouse load. We treat both as one workflow: profile, validate, deduplicate, standardize, impute and monitor.

We work in the tool your team already uses: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn), SQL (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery), R (tidyverse, janitor), Excel and Power Query, Power BI, Tableau Prep, SPSS, Stata and SAS, plus dbt and Great Expectations for automated data quality tests.

Yes. We can deliver Power Query steps that refresh automatically in Excel and Power BI, so cleaning reruns when new data arrives. If you prefer code, we hand over Python, SQL or R scripts instead.

We first diagnose why values are missing, then choose deletion, mean or median, KNN, regression or time-series interpolation. Imputed values are flagged. Outliers are reviewed against domain rules and corrected, capped or kept with a flag, never deleted blindly.

No. We work on copies, keep the raw data untouched and record every transformation in a cleaning log, so each change can be audited, explained or reversed.

It depends on data volume, number of sources and how messy the data is. A free data quality audit gives you a clear scope, timeline and fixed quote before any cleaning starts.

Yes. We can schedule automated checks for completeness, validity, uniqueness and freshness, with alerts and a quality scorecard, so data does not degrade again after cleanup.
